Definition: of uncertain derivation; wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity):--wormwood.
BiblicalUsage: When the third angel sounds, a star falls and its name is Wormwood, and a third of the waters become wormwood, bitter and deadly, so that many men die. The word is a bitter herb, and John makes it the name of a judgment.
TheologicalSignificance: Bitterness that falls from heaven is not an accident, it is a judgment, and it turns sweet water deadly.
